basics.name: Martin Henke
basics.label: Coastal Scientist/Engineer
basics.summary: I am a researcher of engineering background with experience assessing coastal and ocean processes, hazards, and marine renewable energy. With broad experience in a wide range of environments and expertise in the Arctic, I combine cutting-edge research techniques and sound engineering analysis towards informed coastal and oceanic analysis.

work.name: Coastal Science Division, Pacific Northwest National Laboratory
highlights: Produced long-term, high-resolution wave energy hindcasts for nearshore and ice-covered regions of Alaska and analyzed wave-current interaction in the extreme tidal environment of Cook Inlet to derive design conditions supporting tidal power development.

Investigated ice-wave interaction and ice dynamics across the Alaskan Arctic and identified ice hazards affecting coastal and ocean energy infrastructure using numerical simulation, satellite, and observational data.

work.name: Flood Hazards Research Lab, George Mason University
highlights: Developed high-resolution wave and sea ice simulations to assess how declining sea ice affects nearshore extreme wave hazards along Alaskan Arctic coastlines.
Participated in coastal field data collection, including water levels, waves, bathymetry, and vegetation sampling in the Chesapeake Bay.

work.name: University of Alaska Anchorage
highlights: Led independent research resulting in the publication of two academic manuscripts
Managed the thermal and fluids laboratory, coordinating experiments and overseeing equipment
Facilitated thorough and inclusive teaching methods encouraging student learning
Self-taught new and applicable skills, relevant to research needs

projects.name: Arctic Pacific Infrastructure for Sustaining Continuous Engineering and Science (PISCES)
projects.summary: Investigating the impact of wind-waves affecting the seasonal cycle of landfast ice in the Beaufort and Chukchi coastal regions through numerical simulation and analysis of in-situ data.

projects.name: WPTO Alaskan Arctic Wave Resource Assessment Hindcast
projects.summary: Producing and analyzing a high-resolution simulation of Alaskan Arctic wave energy resources in the U.S. Exclusive Economic Zone from 1979–2021.

projects.name: Cook Inlet Wave Model Validation and Site Characterization
projects.summary: Simulating the effects of wave-current interaction in the extreme tidal environment of Cook Inlet, Alaska and deriving design conditions informing tidal power development in the area.

projects.name: NSF NNA: Arctic impacts and reverberations of expanding global maritime trade routes
projects.summary: Collaborated with an inter-disciplinary team to predict future risk of Arctic maritime shipping by assessing how future sea ice loss will affect nearshore extreme wave hazards impacting Alaskan Arctic coastlines.

projects.name: SHORE-BREAK: Assessing and predicting Arctic Coastal Erosion Hazards with ICESat-2
projects.summary: Worked in writing the grant proposal, eventually securing funding for the creation of the project and performed processing of satellite altimetry data yielding transects capable of resolving coastal erosion.

projects.name: Ecological Effects of Sea Level Rise 2019: Quantifying the benefits of natural and nature-based features in Maryland's Chesapeake and Atlantic Coastal Bays
projects.summary: Participated in coastal field data collection, including water levels, waves, bathymetry, and vegetation sampling and built a tool for measuring the effect of vegetation in attenuating coastal waves in numerical simulations.

highlights: Volunteered as a physics and math teacher in a rural Tanzanian school
Reached fluency in the local language, Swahili
Led in the creation and implementation of a grant impacting the health of over 400 students
Utilized minimal resources to create laboratory experiments and demonstrations
